children: Anthony Scaramucci
, founder of
SkyBridge Capital
, declined an early chance to invest $500,000 in
Uber Technologies Inc.
at a $500 million valuation, a stake that would have equaled about 0.1% of the ride-hailing company.

Scaramucci described the decision in a post on X on Friday. He said Uber’s founders visited his office seeking the investment. He said their pitch centered on a stranger in an unfamiliar black car driving his 16-year-old daughter around Manhattan, with the fare charged to his Amex.
"I told them to get the hell out of my office," Scaramucci wrote, adding “I’m not putting my daughter in a car with a stranger.”
Uber did not immediately respond to
request for comments.
I had a chance to invest in Uber, here’s why I didn’t
The Uber founders came into my office with a $500 million valuation and asked me to invest $500,000.
They’re pitch was simple: "An unknown guy, in an unknown black car, will pick up and drive your 16-year-old daughter around…
What the Missed Stake Could Have Been Worth
Scaramucci said that he "totally missed it" and would be retired had he invested.

Uber went public in May 2019 at $45 per share, a fully diluted valuation of roughly $82 billion. A 0.1% stake that was never diluted would be worth about $82 million. In practice, Uber raised capital in many later rounds, which could have reduced an early investor’s ownership percentage.
The former White House Communications Director framed the story as a lesson in venture investing. "You can make a lot of mistakes and still do well," he wrote.

would have grown to $16.5 million, and that he passed after
Warren Buffett
criticized the stock’s valuation.
Trading Metrics
Uber has a market capitalization of $129.60 billion and 2.04 billion shares outstanding. Its 52-week range runs from a low of $92.78 to a high of $63.29.
The large-cap automotive stock has fallen 23.86% over the past 12 months.
